title.en: Define revenue receipts and classify them

say.en: A family earns salary and pays for food, rent and electricity every month. The government also has regular income, like taxes, and regular bills, like salaries and interest. These form the revenue account. What goes in it? In this lesson: Define revenue receipts and classify them.
Distinguish direct and indirect taxes.
Define revenue expenditure with examples.

body.en: *Revenue receipts* are receipts that neither create a liability nor reduce the assets of the government. They are of two kinds. Tax revenue: direct taxes, whose burden cannot be shifted (personal income tax, corporation tax), and indirect taxes, whose burden can be shifted (GST, customs duties, excise duties). Non-tax revenue: interest received on loans given, dividends and profits from public enterprises, fees, fines, and grants received.

points.en: No liability created, no asset reduced
Direct taxes: income tax, corporation tax
Non-tax: interest, dividends, fees, fines, grants

narration.en: Revenue receipts are receipts that neither create a liability nor reduce the assets of the government. They are of two kinds. Tax revenue: direct taxes, whose burden cannot be shifted (personal income tax, corporation tax), and indirect taxes, whose burden can be shifted (GST, customs duties, excise duties). Non-tax revenue: interest received on loans given, dividends and profits from public enterprises, fees, fines, and grants received.
narration.kn: ಆದಾಯ ಸ್ವೀಕೃತಿಗಳು ಸರ್ಕಾರಕ್ಕೆ ಹೊಣೆಗಾರಿಕೆ ಸೃಷ್ಟಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ, ಆಸ್ತಿ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ತೆರಿಗೆ ಆದಾಯ: ನೇರ ತೆರಿಗೆ (ಆದಾಯ ತೆರಿಗೆ, ಕಾರ್ಪೊರೇಟ್ ತೆರಿಗೆ) ಮತ್ತು ಪರೋಕ್ಷ ತೆರಿಗೆ (GST, ಸುಂಕಗಳು). ತೆರಿಗೆಯೇತರ ಆದಾಯ: ಬಡ್ಡಿ, ಲಾಭಾಂಶ, ಶುಲ್ಕ, ದಂಡ, ಅನುದಾನಗಳು.

body.en: *Revenue expenditure* is expenditure that neither creates physical or financial assets nor reduces the liabilities of the government. It covers the normal running of government departments and services: salaries and pensions, interest payments on debt, subsidies, and grants to state governments and other bodies. Grants to states count as revenue expenditure of the Centre even if the states use some of them to create assets.

points.en: No asset created, no liability reduced
Grants to states: *revenue expenditure* of the Centre

say.en: Let us work through this together. Classify each item and find revenue receipts (₹ crore): income tax 1,000; GST 800; dividends from public sector firms 200; fees and fines 100; salaries paid 900; interest paid 400.
Tax revenue: income tax direct 1,000 plus GST indirect 800 equals 1,800.
Non-tax revenue: dividends 200 plus fees and fines 100 equals 300.
Revenue receipts equals 1,800 plus 300 equals 2,100.
Salaries 900 and interest 400 are revenue expenditure (total 1,300), not receipts.
So the answer is Revenue receipts equals 2,100 rupees crore; salaries and interest are revenue expenditure (1,300 rupees crore).
